claims: One full cord is 8 feet (2.44 m) long, by 4 feet (1.22 m) wide, by 4 feet (1.22 m) high.

The formula to convert a set of length, width, and height measurements of a stack of wood in feet to the number of cords of wood is as follows: number of cords = (length (ft) × width (ft) × height (ft)) / 128 ft³.
Or, if you wonder how much is a cord of wood using SI units (meters): number of cords = (length (m) × width (m) × height (m)) / 3.6246 m³.
If the stack consists of the standard 16 inch long logs, and the stack is only one log deep, we call it a face cord of wood.
So a face cord is 8 feet (2.44 m) long, 16 inches (40.6 cm) deep, and 4 feet (1.22 m) high, which is about the amount you'd see stacked up against a log cabin.
For example, outside our log cabin, we stack some standard length firewood, whose length is 7 feet (2.134 m) and height is 4 feet (1.219 m).
For a face cord, the calculator will accept any width measurement, but to be correct, change the units of the width row to inches and enter the number 16.
Cords of wood can weigh anywhere from 2,000 to 5,000 pounds, depending on the type of wood and whether it is green (fresh), seasoned, or kiln-dried firewood.
A quarter cord of wood has a volume of 32 cubic ft or typical dimensions of 4 feet high, 6 feet long, and 16 inches wide (4'×6'×16").
